propositions: Current fixed-threshold compaction (threshold=10) produces quadratic growth in retired snapshot bytes (Θ(N²)) even after the producer defect stops, reaching 344× amplification over the active snapshot at N=8,000 events

Byte/replay-cost-aware cadence (fold when pending_source_bytes >= alpha·active_snapshot_bytes) achieves linear retention (Θ(N)) with tunable amplification factor ≈1/alpha while bounding replayed bytes to alpha fraction of snapshot load

All three cadence candidates (fixed-count control, geometric doubling, byte-cost-aware) preserve ADR 0035 contracts for crash recovery, rebuild-on-stray, conservative horizon, mixed-version rollback, and two-clone union convergence because they change only the WHEN trigger, not snapshot placement or retire/restore rules

Geometric doubling cadence achieves Θ(N) storage but leaves replay tail unbounded in absolute terms (2,880 events at N=8,000), whereas byte-cost bounds read cost to (1+alpha)× unavoidable snapshot load

Adoption requires new config compact.snapshot_alpha with default ≤0 for backward compatibility, an ADR decision gate, and implementation decomposition into separate tasks; no production change is authorized from this research ticket
